issues.description: Using @ts-ignore suppresses all TypeScript errors for the import, hiding potential type safety issues.
issues.suggestion: Remove @ts-ignore and add proper type definitions for 'neverchange' package or create a .d.ts file with type declarations.

issues.description: Database instance is typed as 'any', completely bypassing TypeScript's type safety and making it impossible to catch errors at compile time.
issues.suggestion: Create a proper interface or type for the database instance (e.g., 'interface DBInstance { execute: (sql: string, params?: any[]) => Promise<void>; query: (sql: string) => Promise<any[]>; init: () => Promise<void>; addMigrations: (migrations: Migration[]) => void; }') and type the db variable accordingly.

issues.description: The condition 'if(db) db;' checks if db exists but then does nothing - it doesn't return early. This means initDb() will reinitialize the database and re-run migrations every time it's called.
issues.suggestion: Change to 'if (db) return;' or 'if (db) return db;' to prevent re-initialization.

issues.description: Missing space after 'if' keyword and inconsistent with other code style.
issues.suggestion: Use 'if (db)' with a space for consistency with standard TypeScript formatting.

issues.description: Migration functions use 'any' type for the db parameter, losing type safety.
issues.suggestion: Define a proper type for the migration db parameter to ensure type safety in migration functions.

issues.description: The addTodo function catches errors but doesn't throw them, silently failing and returning undefined. Callers cannot detect if the operation succeeded.
issues.suggestion: Either remove the try-catch to let errors propagate, or re-throw the error after logging: 'throw error;' at the end of the catch block.

issues.description: Console.log statement in production code may clutter logs and is not appropriate for library code.
issues.suggestion: Remove console.log or replace with a proper logging framework that can be configured based on environment.

issues.description: getTodos() doesn't check if db is initialized before use, which could cause a null reference error if called before initDb().
issues.suggestion: Add a null check at the start: 'if (!db) throw new Error("Database not initialized. Call initDb() first.");' or ensure db is properly initialized in all code paths.

issues.description: No input validation on queries. While this specific query is safe, the pattern of not validating inputs is risky.
issues.suggestion: Add validation patterns and consider using a query builder or ORM to prevent SQL injection risks in future code modifications.

issues.description: toggleTodo() has no error handling. If the database operation fails, the error will be unhandled and may crash the application.
issues.suggestion: Add try-catch error handling consistent with other functions, or document that errors should be handled by the caller.

issues.description: toggleTodo() doesn't validate if the id parameter is a valid positive integer, allowing potentially invalid queries.
issues.suggestion: Add input validation: 'if (!Number.isInteger(id) || id <= 0) throw new Error("Invalid todo ID");'

issues.description: toggleTodo() doesn't return any indication of success or number of rows affected, making it impossible to know if the todo existed.
issues.suggestion: Return the result of db.execute() or query for affected rows count to allow callers to verify the operation succeeded.

issues.description: updateTodo() has inconsistent error handling - it logs and re-throws, but addTodo() only logs. This inconsistency makes the API unpredictable.
issues.suggestion: Standardize error handling across all functions - either all should throw or all should return error objects/status codes.

issues.description: updateTodo() doesn't validate the text parameter, allowing empty strings or excessively long text that could cause issues.
issues.suggestion: Add validation: 'if (!text || text.trim().length === 0) throw new Error("Todo text cannot be empty");' and consider a maximum length check.

issues.description: Function doesn't check if the update affected any rows, so calling with a non-existent ID will silently succeed.
issues.suggestion: Check affected rows and throw an error if the todo ID doesn't exist: 'if (result.changes === 0) throw new Error("Todo not found");'

issues.description: No check to prevent updating deleted todos, which could cause data inconsistency.
issues.suggestion: Add 'AND deleted = 0' to the WHERE clause to prevent updating already-deleted todos.

issues.description: Console.log statements in production code (lines 42, 63, 75) should be replaced with proper logging.
issues.suggestion: Use a logging framework that supports different log levels and can be disabled in production.

issues.description: Module-level mutable state (db variable) makes testing difficult and can cause issues in multi-tenant or test scenarios.
issues.suggestion: Consider using a class-based approach or dependency injection pattern to manage database instances, making the code more testable and flexible.

issues.description: toggleTodo() doesn't check the 'deleted' flag, allowing toggling of deleted todos which may be unintended behavior.
issues.suggestion: Add 'AND deleted = 0' to the WHERE clause to prevent operations on deleted todos.

issues.description: DB_NAME is hardcoded, making it difficult to use different databases for testing, development, or multi-tenancy.
issues.suggestion: Accept DB_NAME as a parameter to initDb() or load from environment variables: 'const DB_NAME = process.env.DB_NAME || "todo";'

codeQuality.summary: This database module has several critical issues that need immediate attention. The most severe is the broken initialization check (line 7) that will cause migrations to re-run on every call. The liberal use of 'any' types and @ts-ignore completely defeats TypeScript's safety benefits. Error handling is inconsistent - some functions swallow errors (addTodo), some propagate them (updateTodo, deleteTodo), and one has none (toggleTodo). There's no validation of db initialization state, risking null reference errors. Input validation is absent, and there are no checks for affected rows, making it impossible to detect operations on non-existent records. The module-level mutable state pattern makes testing difficult. Security concerns include lack of input validation patterns and operations that can affect deleted records. While SQL injection is mitigated by parameterized queries, the overall code quality, type safety, and error handling need significant improvement before this code is production-ready.

testCoverage.summary: src/db.ts has zero test coverage. This is a critical database layer with 6 exported functions managing todo CRUD operations and migrations. Key risks: (1) initDb() has a bug on line 7 where 'if(db) db;' does nothing, (2) inconsistent error handling (addTodo swallows errors, updateTodo/deleteTodo throw), (3) no input validation, (4) soft delete pattern untested, (5) migration logic untested. All functions need comprehensive tests covering happy paths, error cases, edge cases (invalid IDs, empty strings), and the soft delete mechanism. Priority: implement tests for initDb migrations, deleteTodo soft delete behavior, and error handling consistency before production deployment.

recommendations.description: Fix broken database initialization guard in src/db.ts line 7. The statement 'if(db) db;' does nothing, causing migrations to re-run on every initDb() call. Change to 'if (db) return;' to prevent re-initialization and potential data corruption.

Add comprehensive test suite for src/db.ts with zero current coverage. Priority tests: (1) database initialization and migrations, (2) soft delete functionality (deleteTodo ensuring data persists with deleted=1 flag), (3) error handling consistency across all CRUD operations.

Replace all 'any' types with proper TypeScript interfaces. Define Database interface for db instance, Migration interface for migration functions, and Todo interface for query results. Remove @ts-ignore directive on line 1 and add proper type definitions.

Standardize error handling across all database functions. Currently inconsistent: addTodo() swallows errors silently, toggleTodo() has no error handling, while updateTodo() and deleteTodo() throw. Decide on a consistent pattern and apply throughout.

Review security and stability of 'neverchange' v0.0.1 dependency. Version 0.0.1 indicates experimental/pre-alpha status. Audit the package code, check for security vulnerabilities, and evaluate if the abstraction over @sqlite.org/sqlite-wasm justifies the risk.

Add input validation to all database operations: (1) validate db is initialized before use in getTodos, toggleTodo, etc., (2) validate todo IDs are positive integers, (3) validate text parameters are non-empty strings, (4) prevent operations on deleted todos by adding 'AND deleted = 0' to WHERE clauses.

Refactor module-level mutable state (db variable) to proper singleton pattern with encapsulation. This will improve testability, enable dependency injection for unit tests, and prevent issues in multi-instance scenarios.

Remove console.log statements from data layer (lines 42, 63, 75) and extract migration configuration to separate function. The data access layer should not contain logging logic - this belongs in the application layer.
